answer: Task assignment hashes the prior epoch's sealed hash with each caller key, so a farm cannot pre-compute which identity gets which prompt. Each key posts an anchor bond locked three epochs, and a submission settles only if its fingerprint differs from every other key the operator runs. Ten cloned keys cost ten bonds plus ten distinct write-ups; a shared answer is caught by fingerprint similarity and slashes the cluster. Per-key reward is capped at the summit one submission earns, so the bond clears cost only when work is real. The sealed hash chain is the crystal: a seed freezes at epoch close.
